newsitem.title: ESTONIA: REPORTED MERGER TALKS DRIVE BOURSE HIGHER.
newsitem.headline: REPORTED MERGER TALKS DRIVE BOURSE HIGHER.

text.p: Reports that Tallinna Pank and
Hoiupank had started informal merger talks pushed share prices
on the Estonian bourse higher on Friday, with Tallinna Pank in
focus, dealers said.
"Tallinna Pank rose to 70 kroons when the bourse opened,
but it drifted back as morning trade progressed," one dealer
said.
"Tallinna's (price) is responding to the news in this
morning's newspaper that some unofficial talks have started,"
he added.
A local business paper said that the two banks had started
informal merger talks.
Hoiupank responded with a statement that it had not started
official talks.
Tallinna bank was 65.05/65.50 kroons compared to Thursday's
close of 63.50 kroons.
Hoiupank was three kroons higher on 154.35/154.50 kroons
with a volume of over three million kroons.
"The bourse remains bullish with this news and the price
should stay higher or be stable," another trader said.
-- David Mardiste, Tallinn newsroom, +372 620 9202,
reuters@reuters.ee
